##


How to complete A2P 10DLC registration for a US phone number


**


Once you get a US number from a virtual provider like Quo, you can call customers right away. But to text customers in the US, you’ll need to complete[A2P 10DLC](https://www.quo.com/blog/what-is-a2p-10dlc/) or US carrier registration:


- **What it is:** A2P 10DLC stands for Application-to-Person 10-Digit Long Code. It’s a standard for business text messaging in the US, used when sending messages from a local virtual number to customers.
- **Why it’s required:** US cell carriers require any business texting through a cloud-based phone provider to complete this verification step. It’s how they filter out spam and protect consumers.
- **How it works with Quo:** You can register directly in your Quo workspace by completing a short form with your business and messaging details. Once approved, you’re ready to start texting customers in the US.

**What is the format of a US phone number?**


A US phone number has 10 digits, split into three parts. Using 415-555-2671 as an example:
– **Area code:** The first three digits, 415, identify the geographic region the number belongs to.
– **Central office code:** The next three digits, 555, narrow it down to a smaller area within that region.
– **Line number:** The last four digits, 2671, identify the specific line.
To call a US number from outside North America, add the country code first: **+1** or **00 1** from countries that use 00 as their international dialing prefix.
